chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who emancipated his slave: 'He is free, with no claim of ownership over him; he is independent, goes his way and may manage his own affairs as he pleases. But if he guarantees his debt/liability, then he inherits him.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: Independent/freeman who goes his own way
key_terms.نَكَّلَ: To emancipate partially or retain a share of value

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a slave who is partially freed but still owes value to the master?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifies the legal status of a slave who is partially emancipated (*nakal*) by retaining a debt (*jarira*) on their labor. It establishes that while the slave gains personal freedom and the right to choose their master, the master retains inheritance rights only until the debt is fully secured or paid, distinguishing this state from full manumission. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the gradual transition of rights and the economic dimensions of emancipation within the family structure.
